claim_tested: A LONRF-family RING at the RING2 position supports intrinsic ubiquitin-ligase activity
key_finding: LONRF2 is a bona fide protein quality control ubiquitin ligase; binds and ubiquitylates abnormally structured TDP-43, hnRNP M1 and artificially misfolded proteins; Lonrf2-/- mice show age-dependent TDP-43-mediated motor neuron degeneration
context: Human/mouse; neurons, iPSC-derived motor neurons, Lonrf2-/- mice
confidence_limitations: High for LONRF2. Transfer to LONRF1 is inference from shared architecture; LONRF2 has only the RING2-position RING, which by this analysis is the RING LONRF1 shares

claim_tested: Which RING residues contact an E2~Ub conjugate
key_finding: RNF4 RING dimer bound to UbcH5A~Ub; E2 contacts map to loop1 (P137/I138), the central helix (C166, D169, S170, N173) and loop2 (P178/T179); R181 bridges E2 and the folded-back donor Ub
context: Rat RNF4 RING, human UbcH5A, ubiquitin; crystal structure
confidence_limitations: High. Used here only to define contact positions for transfer

claim_tested: Generality of the RING E2-binding face
key_finding: BIRC7 (K253/V254, P283/I284, R286) and CBL (K382/I383, P417/F418, R420) use the same three positions; all three references independently map their loop-1 hydrophobic onto LONRF1 G125 and L481
context: Human BIRC7-UBE2D2~Ub; phospho-CBL-UBE2D2
confidence_limitations: High. CBL structure (4A4C) lacks ubiquitin

claim_tested: Is each LONRF1 RING a complete cross-brace RING with an intact E2 face?
key_finding: Both are complete cross-brace C3HC4 zinc sites. RING2 superposes on RNF4 at 0.40 A with E2-face residues displaced 0.61 A and retains L481/P514/K517; RING1 superposes at 0.85 A with 2.19 A face displacement and carries G125 and R156 at the two most constrained E2-contact positions
context: Human LONRF1, AlphaFold model; RING1 mean pLDDT 80.2, RING2 94.3
confidence_limitations: Prediction only. No experimental LONRF1 structure exists; AlphaFold does not model the zinc ions

citation: This analysis (UniProt vertebrate orthologs, n=165 species)
claim_tested: Are the E2-face positions under purifying selection?
key_finding: Mean Shannon entropy at the 10 E2-contact positions: RING2 0.21 bits vs RING1 1.57 bits; RING2 lower at every position (Wilcoxon p=0.0039). L481 100% Leu, P514 99% Pro, K517 99% Lys
context: Vertebrata (fish to mammals), UniProt reference and TrEMBL entries
confidence_limitations: Sequence-database sampling is uneven across clades; register assignment relies on the invariant C-G-H motif

citation: This analysis (AlphaFold zinc-site detection, LONRF2 Q1L5Z9)
claim_tested: Is RING1 required for LONRF-family ligase activity?
key_finding: LONRF2, the experimentally validated ligase, has no cross-brace RING at the RING1 position (only a single 4-Cys cluster C143/C146/C163/C166); its single RING sits at the RING2 position with the same L451/P484/K487 face
context: Human LONRF2
confidence_limitations: Computational; UniProt also annotates only one RING-type zinc finger in LONRF2

claim_tested: Does RING1 function as the second protomer of a RING dimer rather than as an E2-binding RING?
key_finding: RING1+RING2 superpose onto the RNF4 RING dimer at 1.63 A (32 anchors), centroid separation 21.2 A vs 21.3 A (RNF4) and 21.7 A (BIRC7); permutation p<2.5e-4. Modelled interface is sparse (one contact, T135)
context: Human LONRF1 AlphaFold model vs 4AP4 / 4AUQ
confidence_limitations: Model-based; inter-RING PAE 3.3-6.0 A is good but the sparse interface weakens it. LONRF2 works with one RING, so the pairing cannot be obligatory for the family

citation: This analysis (UniProt domain comparison vs LONP1/LONP2)
claim_tested: Does LONRF1 have Lon protease activity?
key_finding: LONRF1/2/3 have only the Lon N-terminal substrate-binding domain; no Lon proteolytic domain, no Walker-A P-loop, no Ser-Lys dyad. LONP1 has all of these (Walker-A at 523, proteolytic 759-949, active sites S855/K898)
context: Human proteins, UniProt annotation plus motif search
confidence_limitations: Database-level plus direct motif search; conclusion is robust

claim_tested: Is an E2 conjugating enzyme a known LONRF1 partner?
key_finding: No UBE2D-family E2 among 86 partners. Only UBE2I (SUMO E2) and UBE2L6 (ISG15 E2), 3 experiments each, high-throughput two-hybrid
context: Human, mostly yeast two-hybrid screens
confidence_limitations: Absence of evidence; Y2H screens are poorly suited to transient E3-E2 contacts

claim_tested: What cellular context does LONRF1 act in?
key_finding: Lonrf1 is ubiquitously expressed; Lonrf1-high liver sinusoidal endothelial cells show NF-kB and p53 pathway activation and suppressed proteasome signalling; no senescence association
context: Mouse single-cell transcriptomics, liver and wound healing
confidence_limitations: Transcriptomic association only; no ligase assay, no substrate

claim_tested: LONRF1 RING2 can physically accept an E2~ubiquitin conjugate
key_finding: Conjugate transferred by zinc-ligand superposition (RMSD 0.40 A); backbone+CB contacts at L1+2 14 atoms vs 18 for RNF4 Ile138 and 21 for BIRC7 Val254
context: Rotamer-independent metric; same procedure applied to 6 RINGs
confidence_limitations: High for geometry; does not demonstrate activity

claim_tested: LONRF1 RING1 has an intact E2-binding face
key_finding: Gly125 at the loop-1 anchor is the only residue in the panel with no CB atom; 10 contact atoms vs 14-21 for all others; Arg156 replaces the loop-2 proline
context: Panel of RNF4, BIRC7, LONRF1 RING1/2, LONRF2, LONRF3 RING1/2
confidence_limitations: High; Gly has no side chain, so the deficit is not a rotamer artifact

claim_tested: The RING1 position carries a conserved second function
key_finding: LONRF1 keeps a cross-brace with Gly125/Arg156; LONRF3 keeps one but loses Pro and linchpin (Ala193/Gly196); LONRF2 has no cross-brace, only C143/C146/C163/C166
context: Geometric detection, pairwise 2.8-5.2 A, centroid radius 1.5-3.3 A
confidence_limitations: High; three different modes of loss indicate relaxed constraint

claim_tested: The LONRF Lys linchpin is non-functional
key_finding: RNF4 Arg181 tips lie 3.82-5.99 A from CB; Lys CB-NZ max 5.07 A over 44 lysines; LONRF1 Lys517 CB sits 5.42 A from donor Ub Gln40 CB vs 5.70 A for RNF4
context: Measured in the same crystal structure
confidence_limitations: High for geometry; predicts reduced efficiency, not loss

claim_tested: The RING1 E2 site is sterically blocked in the folded protein
key_finding: LONRF1 RING1 49 occluding residues vs 2 for RING2, but BIRC7 (known ligase) scored 92; mean PAE 7.6-12.7 A for all occluded cases vs 2.8-3.0 A for free ones
context: Positive control failed
confidence_limitations: Test is uninformative; no conclusion drawn from it

claim_tested: The LONRF1 C-terminal region is a Lon N-terminal substrate-binding domain
key_finding: LONRF1 558-768 vs E. coli Lon N 11-204: TM 0.839, 179 residues under 5 A, RMSD 1.89 A; LONP2 positive control 0.820; negative controls 0.167 and 0.212
context: Sequence-independent alignment, AlphaFold models, controls included
confidence_limitations: High for the fold call; says nothing about client specificity

claim_tested: The three LONRF paralogs share one substrate-recognition module
key_finding: LONRF1 vs LONRF2 Lon-N: TM 0.989, 210 of 210 residues under 5 A, RMSD 0.57 A
context: AlphaFold models
confidence_limitations: High; means LONRF2 substrate data cannot be excluded a priori but is still paralog evidence

claim_tested: The Lon-N domain retains an exposed hydrophobic groove for unfolded clients
key_finding: LONRF1 Lon-N 25.0 percent hydrophobic SASA vs 23.6 for E. coli Lon N, but the LONRF1 TPR array scores highest at 38.4 percent with a 25-residue patch
